explanation: This pole fires retrospectively on the word that opens an explicit two-term scalar comparison: strongest on the exclusive/limiting focus particle after 'not' ('not only / not just / not merely / not simply / not solely X (but also Y)', 2-4 on this pole's scale, the case behind 9 of its 20 top scan examples), and at roughly 0.5-2.5 on the gradable adjective or degree word that a comparative or equative marker scopes over ('as ADJ as', 'as tough a N as', 'twice as ADJ as', 'more/less/equally ADJ than', 'times ADJ-er than', 'as much/well as'). It peaks on that operator or first compared word, decays through the first compared term, and sits at its ~0.1 baseline for bare focus adverbs ('only a game', 'the only option'), bare or merely intensified adjectives ('very/too/so/quite ADJ'), superlatives ('most important', 'biggest'), non-degree comparisons ('similar to', 'same as', 'whereas', 'compared to', 'as' + NP, coordinating 'as well as'), 'at least/at most', and the second comparison term; in code the same slot shows up as the ternary ' ?' (and weakly as ' >').
